task_completion.description: OpenBCI GUI application is launched and visible.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The OpenBCI GUI window is open on the desktop.

task_completion.description: The playback file 'OpenBCI-EEG-S001-EyesOpen.txt' is selected as the data source.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The file selection dialog or the 'Playback File' field in the GUI shows 'OpenBCI-EEG-S001-EyesOpen.txt'.

task_completion.description: The session is started and data is streaming.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Start Session' button has been clicked and the EEG waveform displays are active/moving.

task_completion.description: A recording is initiated and lasts for at least 5 seconds.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Start Recording' button is toggled to 'Stop Recording', and the elapsed recording time or system clock shows a delta of at least 5 seconds before recording stops.

task_completion.description: The recorded file is renamed to 'alpha_calibration.txt' in the specified directory.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A file manager (Nautilus) or terminal window shows the file 'alpha_calibration.txt' exists within '~/Documents/OpenBCI_GUI/Recordings/'.

integrity.description: The agent used the OpenBCI GUI for recording rather than simulating data via script.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with GUI buttons (Start Session, Record) and the live waveform visualization.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply create an empty file named 'alpha_calibration.txt' using 'touch'.
integrity.visual_evidence: The file size or content preview in a file manager should reflect a real EEG data log (multiple columns of numbers), not an empty or 0-byte file.

integrity.description: The agent used the specific playback file requested.
integrity.visual_evidence: The GUI source configuration panel shows the path to 'OpenBCI-EEG-S001-EyesOpen.txt'.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The recording must be at least 5 seconds long.
